title: Where one file lives as it cools
claim: With the recommended lifecycle policy, a file that nobody reads moves to EFS IA after 30 days and to EFS Archive after 90 days.
alt: A timeline of days since the last read: EFS Standard until day 30, EFS IA until day 90, then EFS Archive. A second lane shows that a read resets the timer.
notes: Brief 23; 2-deep.md#cold-files-move-to-cheaper-classes-and-stay-there-unless-you-ask, after the table; caption, no steps. Ticks Day 30 and Day 90 repeat the displays of efs-lifecycle-recommended-defaults-quick-create. The second lane follows efs-lifecycle-transition-based-on-last-access-timer-reset (timer resets when a file in Standard is read) and covers the Standard span only; the figure does not say a read moves a file back to Standard. Axis not to scale. The tick Later only gives the Archive span room; it has no number.
